Bayesian age-period-cohort model (bamp)

Source: R/model-apc_bayes.R
apc_bayes.Rd

Wrapper around the bamp package (Schmid and Held 2007): binomial likelihood for deaths given exposures, logit link, random walk priors of first or second order for age, period and cohort effects, optional overdispersion, MCMC with four chains. Forecasts extrapolate period and cohort effects as random walks for every posterior draw (bamp::predict_apc()), so the draws include parameter uncertainty.

Usage

apc_bayes(
  age = "rw2",
  period = "rw1",
  cohort = "rw1",
  overdispersion = FALSE,
  mcmc = mcmc_control(),
  resolution = c("observed", "grid"),
  shape_years = 5,
  max_refits = 1
)

Arguments

age, period, cohort

Prior for each effect: "rw1" or "rw2". The defaults use first-order random walks for period and cohort: with second-order random walks the extrapolated trends can make forecast intervals span orders of magnitude. First-order random walks carry the last period effect forward without a trend, so forecasts are biased when mortality keeps declining. The vignette "Bayesian age-period-cohort models with bamp" compares both.

overdispersion

Include cell-level overdispersion.

mcmc

MCMC settings from mcmc_control().

resolution

"observed" or "grid".

shape_years

Number of recent years used for the shape factors.

max_refits

Refits with longer chains if not converged.

Value

A model specification.

Details

The wrapper makes bamp behave like every other model:

  • Resolution. With resolution = "observed" (default) the model is fitted where the deaths were observed: 5-year age groups with annual periods use periods_per_agegroup = 5 (Knorr-Held and Rainer 2001). Exposures are aggregated to the death cells. Age groups must have equal widths; an open last group is treated as one more group of that width.

  • Grid. Draws for age groups are mapped to the modelling grid with age-specific shape factors (single-year rate relative to its group rate, exposure-weighted to 1 within each group) estimated from the preprocessed training data of the last shape_years years. Use step_ungroup() in prep when deaths are grouped.

  • Convergence. bamp::checkConvergence() is called explicitly; a stratum that has not converged is refitted with twice as many iterations up to max_refits times, then reported as failed in the diagnostics.

  • Integers. bamp needs whole numbers; deaths and exposures are rounded and the largest relative rounding change is recorded.

Heterogeneity variants ("rw1+het", "rw2+het") are not offered because bamp::predict_apc() does not forecast them in bamp 3.0.0.

Draws are posterior draws of the rates. Predictive draws (mt_forecast(predictive = TRUE)) add Poisson variation of the deaths given the rates of each draw and the exposures, as for the other models of expected rates; no other observation noise is added. bamp's binomial likelihood and its overdispersion term (overdispersion = TRUE) are not carried into the predictive draws: the overdispersion only enters the posterior of the rates. If intervals are too narrow on real data, that is a property of the model (see recalibrated(), ensemble(), or overdispersed models such as stanmomo(family = "nb")).

References

Knorr-Held L, Rainer E (2001). Prognosis of lung cancer mortality in West Germany: a case study in Bayesian prediction. Biostatistics 2(1): 109-129.

Schmid VJ, Held L (2007). Bayesian age-period-cohort modeling and prediction: BAMP. Journal of Statistical Software 21(8): 1-15. doi:10.18637/jss.v021.i08

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("bamp", quietly = TRUE)) {
  x <- mt_example(years = 2005:2019)
  fit <- mt_fit(apc_bayes(mcmc = mcmc_control("test")), x, prep = mt_prep(step_ungroup()))
  fc <- mt_forecast(fit, h = 5, n_draws = 200, seed = 1)
}
# }
